problem: The population $P(t)$ of mice in a forest varies according to the differential equation ${P}^{′}(t)=rP(t),$ where $t$ is the time, measured in months from the start of the observation period, and $r>0.$  It is known that the mouse population quintuples (increases fivefold) after the first two months. How long does it take for the mouse population to increase eightfold from the start of the observation period? Round your answer to one decimal place.

activity_context.topic_title: Exponential Growth and Decay Models With First-Order ODEs: Calculating Unknown Times and Initial Values
